title: QBR - Verdant Systems Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focusing on usage growth, a recent cost spike driven by batch jobs, a minor reliability blip in early Sept, and alignment on roadmap + reserved capacity options. Agreed next steps include pricing proposal for reserved capacity, performance microbenchmarks, and follow-up on compliance questions.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share updated pricing and reserved capacity proposal by 2025-09-30
Maya Patel: Run performance microbenchmarks on v3.1 quantized model and share results by 2025-10-07
Priya Shah: Confirm priority PII data flows and compliance needs by 2025-09-29
Noah Reed: Provide recent incident logs and SLO breach details by 2025-09-26
next_steps: Redwood to send reserved capacity pricing and recommended configs
Schedule deeper technical deep-dive on on-prem/private deployment (if required)
Customer to provide sample slow traces and incident logs
Set up cost alerts and a shared dashboard link
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-23
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Liam Torres (Verdant CFO); Priya Shah (Verdant Head of ML); Noah Reed (Verdant Platform Eng)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR for Verdant Systems, appreciate you making time. i'll run through a couple slides and then pass to maya for the reliability bits.
[00:20] Liam (Verdant): yeah thanks jordan, quick heads up, i'm juggling a CFO call so priya/noah will drive most of the tech questions.
[00:30] Jordan: totally, we'll keep it high level. first item, usage trends — we've seen a 42% month-on-month growth in token consumption from verdant since june, most of which is driven by nightly batch reranks and a new summarization feature you rolled out. do those numbers track with what you see?
[00:50] Priya: yeah that tracks, the summarizer we shipped in july started to push a lot more tokens. we did some large batch runs for historical data in mid-aug, that was a big chunk of the spike.
[01:05] Noah: to add, we also increased the max tokens per request for the agent pipeline from 1k to 2k in august to handle longer context, so that inflated consumption.
[01:20] Jordan: ok good context. on cost — you flagged a cost spike in the first week of september, we dug in and it looks like three scheduled batch jobs overlapped and a few misconfigured retries caused duplicated payloads. maya, want to summarize what we found?
[01:38] Maya (Redwood): sure, we pulled the call traces — there were repeated retries originating from the job runner; requests were small but repeated, and because of prefect-style batch concurrency you got multiplied token counts. the platform normally de-dupes a bit but in that run the job IDs changed so the cache wasn't used. also you were on shared hosted tier and hit a token-rate cap, so some requests retried client-side.
[02:05] Priya: ugh yeah we saw the retries, we thought it was a network glitch. should've caught it earlier.
[02:12] Jordan: actionable there: we recommended adding a job dedupe layer and setting up cost alerts; we've also suggested switching those large nightly jobs to a dedicated reserved instance to get predictable unit pricing.
[02:25] Liam: pricing — we need a clear delta between hosted and reserved. can you send an apples-to-apples doc?
[02:32] Jordan: absolutely, i'll send a reserved capacity proposal with expected cost savings at your current and projected throughput, also include a breakeven calc given your increased tokens.
[02:40] Liam: great.
[02:43] Jordan: maya, reliability incident recap?
[02:46] Maya: yes — in early sept you had a short SLO breach, about 18 minutes of elevated p95 latency; root cause was a transient kernel upgrade on the node pool handling your tenant in the us-west region. our fallback policy kicked in but because you were pinned to a specific model variant with a larger KV cache, warming the fallback caused some extra memory pressure. we resolved within 18 minutes; no data loss.
[03:15] Noah: we have the incident logs, i'll drop those in the shared folder. i wanted to ask about canary/rollouts — if we pin to a model version can you guarantee graceful fallback?
[03:26] Maya: yes we recommend a canary-first rollout with auto-fallback to a smaller variant. thats what we support in dedicated too, and you can configure automatic fallbacks based on latency thresholds. there's a doc link i'll share: https://redwood.ai/docs/fallbacks (note: transcribed link may be approximate).
[03:44] Priya: what about quantized models — we've seen small quality regressions on 4-bit in the internal evals, any guidance?
[03:52] Maya: expected tradeoff, we can run microbenchmarks on v3.1 quantized and compare perplexity+downstream metric on your eval set. our optimize team suggests 8-bit for production summarization for now, 4-bit for cheap experiments.
[04:12] Jordan: and if you go dedicated with reserved capacity, quantization profiles and kernel selection are something we can tune per workload.
[04:20] Liam: security/compliance — priya mentioned PII flows. what do we need for SOC2 + KMS?
[04:28] Jordan: for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC-only control plane. for hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit, and SOC2 certs — i'll drop our security pack.
[04:38] Priya: we need explicit data residency options for EU processing for a subset of our customers. possible?
[04:44] Jordan: yes, we have region pinning and private VPCs in eu-west; for full residency we can discuss a private deployment.
[04:51] Noah: quick question — what's the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:55] Maya: hosted has a best-effort SLA for latency but an uptime SLO; Dedicated gets SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on contract tier. i'll send the SLA matrix.
[05:06] Priya: on observability, can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route? that's essential for us to allocate costs to product teams.
[05:14] Jordan: yes, the console has per-route dashboards, and we'll share a dashboard link that you can grant view access to your product leads.
[05:20] Liam: ok, other asks — we want a small pilot of Reserved for one of our internal services, 3 months. can you outline the minimal commit?
[05:29] Jordan: yes, typical minimal commit for a pilot is 3-6 months and a small GPU pool; i'll put formal numbers in the proposal.
[05:35] Maya: one more technical note — the batch rerank pipeline would benefit from KV cache tuning and prefix caching; that alone should cut token cost by ~15-25% for repeated context.
[05:47] Priya: that's huge if it's real. can you show an example config?
[05:50] Maya: sure, i'll include config snippets and a before/after estimate.
[05:55] Noah: on incident logs — i'll upload them to the shared drive now, link will be in the follow-up email.
[06:00] Jordan: excellent. recap of next steps: jordan to send reserved capacity pricing & breakeven by sept 30; maya to run perf microbenchmarks and KV cache tuning examples and share by oct 7; noah to upload incident logs by sept 26; priya to confirm compliance/residency requirements by sept 29.
[06:22] Liam: makes sense, thanks for the clear action list.
[06:25] Priya: thanks all, appreciate the recommendations.
[06:28] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the proposal and a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive next week.
[06:34] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: some vendor/product names transcribed incorrectly in spots (e.g., 'prefect' as 'perfect', 'KV cache' occasionally 'K V cache'), timestamps are approximate. Links referenced are shorthand and will be shared in follow-up email.
